notes.content:
Crave for more stories from the Coffee Talk customers?
[b]Toge Productions and Chorus Worldwide together are brewing a new spin-off story of Coffee Talk![/b]

[previewyoutube=m7a7og3e4fY;full][/previewyoutube]

Coffee Talk Tokyo is the next installment of the Coffee Talk series. It will take you to an all-new - but strangely familiar - all-night coffee shop, this time in a Tokyo backstreet. With a cast of new characters (and one or two familiar faces), Coffee Talk Tokyo will introduce you to new themes and storylines.

Once again taking on the role of Barista, you will take drink orders from customers like Kenji, a traditional kappa salaryman facing a life of retirement, Vin, the Barista’s assistant struggling with the daily consequences of a past catastrophe, and Ayame, a spunky ghost trying to move on with her (after)life.

notes.title: Coffee Talk 2nd Anniversary!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/19d6fadbd789e784139a51341d2f1913cccde837.png[/img]

Greetings, fellow Cafe Regulars. 

Happy second year anniversary to Coffee Talk, the game we all know and love!
Especially to you all Cafe Regulars who've been with us, we are truly thankful for your support. We've been through a lot together, lots of great memories, and we feel like we could connect with you all through Coffee Talk.

After two years, there are many things that we have achieved together. Let's take a look, shall we? 

[h2]Coffee Talk finally open for business in 2020... [/h2]
Coffee talk was released two years ago, exactly on [b]January 29 2020.[/b] It's such a big day for us where we released Coffee Talk simultaneously on different PC platforms and consoles! The game was well-received by many players around the world. A few months after, we announced [url=https://twitter.com/coffeetalk_game/status/1255149778129879040?s=20]the Coffee Talk Collector's Edition[/url] with the help from our friends at [url=https://store.strictlylimitedgames.com/collections/coffee-talk]Strictly Limited Games and Chorus Worldwide.[/url] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/643caf05383c0f559949cd6cb9d0bb790a9854c1.png[/img]
[i]Coffee Talk collector's edition and all the goodies![/i]

There are lots of players who love the music of Coffee Talk, thus we decided to release the [url=https://twitter.com/coffeetalk_game/status/1318567650361069571]LP record of Andrew Jeremy's Coffee Talk greatest hits[/url] back in [b]October 2020, [/b]in collaboration with [url=https://blackscreenrecords.com/products/coffee-talk-official-soundtrack]Black Screen Records.[/url]. Everyone just loves vibing to Lo-Fi Hip Hop soundtrack while relaxing or just doing stuff, don't you think? ;)

[i][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/19b70143f17b2b190241a6d6ec9885c7d029550a.png[/img]
The vinyl came with the [url=https://twitter.com/blackscreenrec/status/1463462847153946624?s=20]Matcha Green and Coffee Brown double combo![/url][/i]

A few months after the vinyl release, we announced the[url=https://sanshee.com/collections/coffee-talk] first official Coffee Talk merchandise and collectibles[/url] on Sanshee in [b] December 2020.[/b] You were able to [url=https://twitter.com/TeamSanshee/status/1334210039247200258/photo/1]get it in a bundle[/url] if you want to collect everything on the list!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/199252fa630fbed71a31e9924cdb7926047f19f1.png[/img]
[i]What a gorgeous bundle of collectibles~[/i]

[h2]Coffee Talk continued to strive even better in 2021! [/h2]

During our first anniversary in [b]January 2021,[/b] we added mod support to the game. It was a big milestone for us to support the dedicated players, where localization and voice over mod were implemented! This is a mod that really brings more opportunity to our community. They can took part in adding their own language support and custom voice overs so more people can enjoy Coffee Talk as well!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/8525d05022f317fc6a1ce74bbdb6ce342d1e1126.gif[/img]

In the same month as the first anniversary of Coffee Talk, we were chosen as the finalist [b][i]Outstanding Achievement for an Independent Game[/i][/b] during [url=https://sea.ign.com/sea-indie-games/168111/news/coffee-talk-is-sole-southeast-asian-game-nominated-for-dice-awards]the 24th D.I.C.E Award[/url] back in [b]January 2021?[/b] It's a huuuge achievement for us to be recognized at such an grand event.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/9eeab1cd18210ccfefe95a26362ce6e4cf811684.png[/img]

The Coffee Talk OST Vinyl we released back in 2020 got a repress in [b]April 2021![/b] Not only that, Black Screen Records also released another version [url=https://blackscreenrecords.com/products/coffee-talk-original-soundtrack]of a beautiful 2xCD set[/url], definitely a treat for those who don't have a turntable. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/66223ebfb32e786a6ea7b47b68f28d74c49bd535.png[/img]
[i]The 2xCD set contain 22 tracks and 2 bonus tracks![/i]

In the SEA Game Awards Level Up KL 2021, we won the Grand Jury Award! If you didn't know, SEA Game Awards is one of the biggest game nomination event in Southeast Asia, and that's already a huge achievement for us as an indie game developer! We were just as amazed as everyone else when we watched the nomination back in [b]November 2021![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/6f0b9d06eb0777d74e0f31410ea089e3b95a22bf.png[/img]

The overwhelming support of the players for the past years pushed us even higher, and we finally did it! Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly were officially announced with a trailer back in [b]September 2021[/b] during [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iYCrI-GbJzA]the Indie Houses Direct.[/url] The new episode is considered as a standalone title that will be released on PC and consoles. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qCE1S4i90s
[i]The announcement was kinda unexpected, but the community loves it![/i]

Did you hear of the Freya plush Campaign few months ago? The campaign ended with a success and [url=https://twitter.com/coffeetalk_game/status/1479105484347121665] and 305 Freya plushies were  sent across the world![/url] A very huge thanks to [url=https://www.makeship.com/products/freya-plush]Makeship[/url] for supporting the campaign back in [b]October 2021. [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/af4da18eda2d90d058d17d0207fa7f580bb4b8e6.png[/img]
[i]The initial design back in 2020 (left) and the final design 2021 (right) for the Freya plush.[/i]

[h2]Coffee Talk in 2022 and beyond. [/h2]

Our journey is not over yet, there's still much to do! There are many exciting events and updates to be expected this year. Let's hope for the best and look forward to the next Episode of Coffee Talk! Once again, please take care of us this year as well~

On this second anniversary, we have another wonderful gift for you all!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33359823/8f7e9bab748e40c1ee2db1b4ead6a37ac6dd8ebf.png[/img]

[b]The Coffee Talk - 2 Years Anniversary Wallpaper is free to download![/b] 
You can get them in a [url=https://bit.ly/ct-anniv2022]better resolution for desktop and phone.[/url] Much thanks to [url=https://twitter.com/locoberi01]Locoberi[/url] to create this special anniversary wallpaper!

[h3]Feel free to try out the Coffee Talk Episode 2 Demo![/h3]
During the Coffee Talk Anniversary, you can try out the Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus and Butterfly Demo! You can only access it during Lunar New Year Steam Sale.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1663220/Coffee_Talk_Episode_2_Hibiscus__Butterfly/


Please stay safe and healthy, friends!
Fully brewed with love,

Coffee Talk Team. ːctluaː

notes.title: Coffee Talk Devlog #4: Brewing the Gameplay Mechanics and Latte Art Feature
notes.content:
What makes Coffee Talk different from other visual novels out there? The immersive coffee-making experience, of course.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/a683635ed0593201506dd432a4a852c9873d5a4a.png[/img]

In Coffee Talk, you will play the role of a barista, who run your own cafe that opens at night. There, you will meet people (mostly non-human) and serve them warm drinks — just like what you would expect in a coffee shop. As you help them soothe their souls with a cup of warm drink or two, stories will be unveiled.

•••

In Coffee Talk’s initial stage of development, there has been a continuous debate about how players should enjoy the game. Unlike other games from Toge Productions that are mechanics-heavy, Coffee Talk’s [url=https://togeproductions.itch.io/project-green-tea-latte]prototype[/url] was a straight-up visual novel with minimum gameplay. To make it become more of a “game”, the team then experimented more on the game mechanics.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/1a917feed135302de9fe56b5e58db1cde944910d.gif[/img]

Before, the branching and brewing mechanics were pretty straightforward with predetermined combinations, and players were not able to see whether they made the right drink or not before serving it. However, in the newer version, the game automatically generates the name, visuals, and stats of the beverages, which then became the key to the branching mechanism — it will be further covered in this log.

Read more about the history of Coffee Talk here:  [url=https://togeproductions.itch.io/coffee-talk/devlog/44272/devlog-1-how-the-game-came-to-be-the-seed-the-anxiety-and-the-belief-of-design-by-subtraction]Devlog #1: How the game came to be - The seed, the anxiety, and the belief of design by subtraction[/url]

•••

[h1]Prototype Version vs. Newer Version[/h1]

Even until today, the gameplay mechanics are still being improved. To understand more about that matter, we are going to need the experts in the field. For that reason, I invited [url=https://twitter.com/fredriklauw]Fredrik Lauwrensius[/url] and [url=https://twitter.com/FujiwaraLunasa]Jovan Anggara[/url], the programmers of Coffee Talk as the special guests for this development log!

Both of them joined the team at a different time. While Jovan has been involved ever since the making of the prototype version — which was during the 2017 game jam, Fredrik came aboard about 1–2 weeks later, after some intense discussion about the game mechanism, direction, and so forth. There were many questions lingering for quite some time about Coffee Talk’s game mechanics when this log is still in draft form. Due to me being a complete noob on programming stuff, they are luckily kind enough to explain in a simple way.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/0e3db44b4fbb9bcbd841d525df275d6e0e8f35f6.gif[/img]
 
Jovan told me that in the game jam version, players can freely add any ingredients for a drink. However, it resulted in a massive amount of beverages combinations that could be made, with most of it categorized as “failed” drinks. The team then decided that there should be no failed drink, and therefore tried to limit the possibility of combinations by determining certain ingredients to be used at certain times.

Other than that, players were also able to make cold drinks by adding ice before. The feature was eliminated and a brand new drink statistics was set up. Now the barista will only serve warm drinks containing these 4 statuses: warm/cool/sweet/bitter — because some drinks can tastes sweet and bitter at the same time, and the sensations of warmness and coolness can be experienced at just split seconds apart. The statistics, according to Fredrik and Jovan, affects the branching mechanics where it could cause not only changes in dialogue but also in the later parts of the game.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/ca2eee290c3bf76feec5af8637ede85b2c1448ac.png[/img]
[i]Sneak peek: the newest brewing UI that is currently under development[/i]

•••

[h1]Art in a Cup: Additional yet Significant Feature[/h1]

What is it that could complement a nice, warm drink? We are thinking that latte art would be a nice touch. In Coffee Talk, in addition to serving drinks, players can also add their own latte art for milk-based beverages (or any beverages that use milk as an ingredient). The idea of the feature first came from our beloved CEO, [url=https://twitter.com/kerissakti/status/1097699471457058816]Kris Antoni[/url]. It was not long after I joined Toge Productions that I saw the whole studio burst with enthusiasm toward this particular feature.

Frederik and Jovan said that it took them about a week to make that feature from scratch. Initially, they paid more attention to what the players can do in the development, such as pouring the milk and etching, until they studied the [i]real[/i] latte art… from youtube videos. As time goes by, after many trials, they realized that they should also pay attention to fluid simulation — in short, the consistency and the flow of milk when it is poured.

“The biggest challenge would be to find the right configuration between the consistency of both the drink and the milk,” they said to me after thinking for quite some time. “Aside from it, we also need to think about optimization for this feature because it takes up loads of performance.”

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/ec9d3a90d61f8b1047ceb24589cc67da3677cf98.gif[/img]
 
The game mechanics and latte art feature have been revamped several times until today, even the programmers have lost count. You can give support to the developers by playing the demo and adding it to your wishlist here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/914800/Coffee_Talk/

Also, don't forget to follow Coffee Talk’s [url=https://twitter.com/coffeetalk_game]twitter[/url] for more updates!

Thank you for reading! ☕

notes.title: Devlog #1: How the game came to be - The seed, the anxiety, and the belief of design by subtraction
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/67e168537fee944063ee5a546066afec05a75086.png[/img]
It was a cold rainy night. I was working on a press release while browsing in front of the computer in my room. Just like any other night, I made a cup of something warm to drink to calm my senses and relax my body. That night it was a cup of green tea latte. During one of my short breaks to take a sip and stare out the window, I thought, “this is such a nice calm experience, I wish there were a game that simulated this feeling.” Then the thought came. If I couldn’t find a game like that, I could make one. And thus was born the idea of a game known simply as “Coffee Talk.”

[h1]The game jam that started it all[/h1]
Before we go further, let me tell you a bit about us. My name is Mohammad Fahmi and I’m part of Toge Productions, an indie game developer and publisher based in Indonesia. We were founded in 2009 by two game-loving people (and have since grown to 14), and are mostly known for our hit title, Infectonator. I am the writer and designer of [i]Coffee Talk[/i], but my primary job at Toge is to handle the marketing and PR, and because we are also a publisher with a total of ten games we’re working on, the task is steep.

One of the best things about working at Toge is our annual game jam. At the end of the year, we hold a two week long internal game jam where anyone can make anything. A programmer wants to try making a GDD and concept art for a game? Please do! An artist wishes to take a break from using their drawing tablet and create a board game with traditional watercolor art? No one will stop you! A marketing and PR person wants to make a game about serving green tea latte or coffee to a freelance illustrator elf in the middle of the night? Just do it!

And that’s what happened during the game jam in the second week of December 2017. I pitched the idea that had been brewing in my mind for months prior. A game about serving warm drinks in a cafe that only opens at night, located in a metropolitan city where creatures like orcs become programmers, succubi become business development managers for trading companies, and humans…well, humans do the things we know they always do.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/71f16f8f17bbceb419804ffd191f98b77ab2463b.png[/img]
The main selling points of the game would be its story, its pixel art with 90s anime-inspired graphics, and its lo-fi chill-hop tunes that became so popular suddenly on YouTube that year. There was no title for the game yet, so we called it [i]Project Green Tea Latte[/i]. During the two week game jam, prototypes were made, art was drawn, teams were changed, and in the end we had four prototypes. You can check out all of them here. After the game jam, the studio decided to work on two games at once, and one of them is [i][url=https://togeproductions.itch.io/project-green-tea-latte]Project Green Tea Latte[/url][/i].

[quote][b]Intermezzo:[/b] Before going with Coffee Talk, we came up with a lot of titles, and one that stood out the most was “Things We Talk About at Night.” We loved it, but the title was too long, and localizing it to other languages would be required to release in non-English speaking countries like China or Japan. A shorter title was needed. Thus “Coffee Talk” was born.[/quote]

[h1]The anxiety of not-a-game[/h1]
One of the things that worried us most through the first half of the development was gameplay. Toge has been making games for almost a decade, but all of them have been mechanics heavy. None of them play like [i]Coffee Talk[/i], which is primarily narrative based and text-driven. 

Debates regarding how players should enjoy the game were frequent and plentiful. As the writer and designer of the game, I believed that story and vibe are the core experience that we needed to focus on.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33359823/4adf4078fa75702818910d428bf11cda45c3c7f9.png[/img]
But we also had our doubts. Can we call [i]Coffee Talk[/i] a game when there’s no consequences or skills required to experience it? Categorizing the game as a visual novel was the most natural solution we could think of, but this proved problematic because our fans largely follow us due to the “gameplay” in our games.

We decided to change the game’s branching narrative and brewing mechanics to better quench these worries. The game jam version has very straightforward brewing and branching mechanics, where all the combinations are predetermined. The new version’s mechanics, however, will work differently. While every concoction will result in some kind of drink, the game will automatically generate the name, visuals, and stats of most beverages, which will be the key to the branching mechanism.

Each drink will have four stats: sweetness, bitterness, warmness, and coolness. You might think that it would be better to have only two stats, in which the value determines whether the drink is sweet or bitter, warm or cold - we thought of this, too - but as weird as it sounds, some drinks can give you that feeling of sweetness and bitterness at the same time, or the sensations of warmness and coolness split seconds apart. 

[h1]Design by Subtraction[/h1]
Even with the changes mentioned above, we were still plagued with concerns. This changed when we went to BitSummit to showcase our other games and met the fine folks of Sukeban Games, the developer of [i]VA-11 HALL-A[/i].

During a party on a river bank in Kyoto, we talked about how Sukeban achieved what they have from [i]VA-11 HALL-A[/i]. One thing they told me to keep in mind was not to add features just because you can or because you don’t think the gameplay is deep enough to be called a game. If it has achieved the messages you want to convey, then stop there. Focus on things that matter and don’t force in things that, in the end, will only reduce the quality of the experience you want to deliver.

Our interaction hit me hard. I never mentioned our anxiety about the lack of gameplay in [i]Coffee Talk[/i] and yet here they were, telling me that the first thing I needed to make sure of was something we’d been thinking a lot about for the past few months. We didn’t even showcase [i]Coffee Talk[/i] at BitSummit, but I have to say that amongst all of our games, it was one of the few that made the trip so worthwhile. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AmSBIyT0ih0
The discussion also triggered my memory of one of the best videos by Mark Brown, the six minute and fifty seconds essay about [i]Ico[/i] and the “Design by Subtraction” philosophy coined by Fumito Ueda. In the video, Brown talks about how sometimes you don’t need to add more things to make your game feel more wholesome, taking examples not only from [i]Ico[/i] itself, but also from how [i]Ico[/i] inspired other popular games such as [i]Fez, Journey[/i], and even [i]The Last of Us[/i]. So, while it may sound strange, it’s safe to say that [i]Ico[/i] heavily inspired games like [i]Coffee Talk[/i].
[quote]Because it’s easy to add features that you think are cool or will increase the game length or give you another bullet point in your Steam description. Or is it just diluting the core message of your game, and hurting your ability to have your game be about something, to say something, to resonate.
- Mark Brown[/quote]

[h1]What’s next?[/h1]
We’ve been working on [i]Coffee Talk[/i] for a few months now, and the warm and kind responses from the people who have played the demo have definitely boosted our motivation to finish the game and present you all with a full experience.

For now, we’re going to continue working on the game while giving you updates in the form of social media posts on our Twitter and devlog. In the meantime, take a sip of coffee and tell us what you like or don’t like about the demo.
